orphanCandidates.enumerates: The two types a cost object approval step can be based on - the setting that DECIDES which half of the Authorized Approval Limits window is authoritative, but which is not itself set anywhere on this page. Verbatim lead-in: "A cost object approval step can be based on either:" followed by two bulleted members. This is a genuine two-member enumeration, complete, in source order, nothing sampled.
orphanCandidates.whyNoOwner: NO FIELD ON THIS PAGE OWNS IT, and attaching it to a neighbour would be a false wiring of exactly the kind this run exists to prevent. The nine fields on the Authorized Approval Limits roster are authorized_approval_limits_link, hierarchy_level_selector, can_approve_exception, approval_limit_currency_window, approval_limit_amount, cost_object_approval_level, authorized_approver_checkbox, manager_approval_limit and approval_limit_currency_branch_a; none of them is a limit-vs-level TYPE selector. The type is a property of the cost object approval step / cost object configuration, not of the per-approver record this window writes. user-administration-8b167b96.md states the consumption relationship outright: "The cost object configuration defines the type—either limit or level." and, in the same Note, "If you complete both areas in this window—the Approval Limit area and the Level field—Concur Invoice will use the one that applies to your configuration and ignore the other." So this enumeration is the CONTEXT for a precedence rule between two of this page's fields (approval_limit_amount + approval_limit_currency_window on the one hand, cost_object_approval_level on the other) - it is not a list of options either of them offers. Emitting it as a value set with contextField would require inventing an owner field, which the brief forbids. The full member definitions, verbatim from b335cf33: "Level: This type of approval is defined by each approver's sequential position in the approval process." and "Limit: This type of approval is based on the amount that an approver is authorized to approve (also known as _signing authority_)." Note also that employee-import-e28f2294.md calls the same two things HIERARCHY TYPES rather than approval-step types - "For the Limit hierarchy type, you will use the 710 Cost Object Approver record set to import the approval limit and the currency." - a wording difference recorded, not reconciled.
orphanCandidates.whatWouldFixIt: A built page carrying the cost object approval STEP configuration (the Workflows cost object approval step, or a Cost Object Approval configuration surface) with a field whose documented label is the limit-vs-level type selector. The Workflows page is already built with 114 fields but carries no such type field in this graph, so there is currently nothing legal to wire to. Until such a field exists, the correct home for this fact is the page-level precedence contradiction/dependency already recorded against cost_object_approval_level and approval_limit_amount - NOT a value set. Do not resolve it by minting a type field on Authorized Approval Limits.

Lead-in verbatim: "The company adds the proper authorized approver rights to users using:" then three bullets, complete and in source order.
values: The Authorized Approvers tab in Workflows.
orphanCandidates.whyNoOwner: This is a ROUTE enumeration, not a field-option enumeration - it names three admin surfaces, not three values any control on this page offers. It is recorded here so a later pass does not re-discover it and mistake it for a missed option list. It matters to the boundary this run draws: one of the three routes IS this page ("User Admin"), one is the already-built Workflows page ("The Authorized Approvers tab in Workflows.", i.e. the tab carrying field.workflows.authorized-approver-approval-limit, field.workflows.authorized-approver-level, field.workflows.authorized-approver-can-approve-exception and field.workflows.authorized-approver-list-approver), and one - the employee import - is a surface this corpus cannot support because it defers to the external Shared: Employee Import Specification. Wiring these as values of any field would assert that a control on this window offers a choice of surface, which no file says.
orphanCandidates.whatWouldFixIt: Nothing at the value-set layer; it is already correctly represented as dependency/boundary edges rather than as values. It stays here only as an explicit negative finding.

orphanCandidates.enumerates: NOT AN ENUMERATION - a DECLARED DOMAIN, logged here so it is not mistaken for a missed value set on a later pass. employee-import-e28f2294.md record set 710 Cost Object Approver states the only value domains this corpus gives for the amount/currency pair that this window writes: field 15 Approval Limit is "Numeric", "Specified in the approval limit currency.", "If used, then Approval Limit Currency Code below is required."; field 16 Approval Limit Currency Code is "3 characters" and "Can be either three-digit or three-letter currency code; must be a valid currency in the list of system (reimbursement) currencies".
orphanCandidates.whyNoOwner: Owners EXIST on this page - approval_limit_amount and approval_limit_currency_window (branch B), manager_approval_limit and approval_limit_currency_branch_a (branch A) - so this is deliberately NOT filed as an ownerless catalogue. It is filed here because it is not enumerable and therefore must not become a value set or a validValuesAddition. (a) "Numeric" and "3 characters" are TYPE/LENGTH declarations, not selectable values; materialising them as an unconditional value set would tell a driver those strings are legal entries. (b) The currency list itself is NEVER enumerated anywhere in this corpus - not on this window, not on Workflows, not in the import table; the domain is given only by reference ("the list of system (reimbursement) currencies"), so a driver must read the rendered list at runtime and no currency code may be invented into this graph. (c) The amount is an OPEN numeric domain; the corpus documents only two special values with semantics - "You can enter 0 in the Amount field." / "You can enter 0 in the Manager Approval Limit field." (0 = in the approver chain, no final authority) and "For an unlimited approval amount, leave blank (null)." corroborated by "a limit amount of null will result in an unlimited approval/no limit approval amount." - and writing validValues [0, blank] would falsely assert those are the only legal entries. All four owner fields already carry these facts in their roster notes, verbatim and correctly attributed, which is the right channel. Recorded once here so the absence of a value set on this page reads as a decision, not an oversight. Boundary note: the built Workflows sibling for the same underlying per-approver value is field.workflows.authorized-approver-approval-limit (label "Approval Limit"), which collapses currency+amount into one control and carries no value set either; nothing here is re-homed to it.
orphanCandidates.whatWouldFixIt: Only a documented enumeration of the reimbursement-currency list would turn the currency half into a legitimate value set, and this corpus contains none. The amount half can never become a value set - it is an open numeric domain by documentation. No action; this is a documentary gap, not a defect.
